system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platform
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience building and operating production data platforms and
cloud warehouses for e-commerce, logistics and payments. Hands-on experience with Python, SQL,
Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, Redshift and AWS. Delivered reliable batch and streaming pipelines at
scale, improved data quality through testing and data contracts, and built reusable tooling for
engineering teams. Values well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and trusted analytical warehouses.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace) | 03/2022 -
Present
• Own the ingestion and orchestration layer of the company data platform: approximately 140
Airflow DAGs loading data from Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake.
• Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into 420+ dbt models, with tests on every model;
reduced nightly warehouse build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.
• Introduced JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product teams and the data team,
reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately 9 per month to approximately 2 per month.
• Designed and built a Kafka-based shipment events pipeline processing approximately 30 million
events per day, with p95 end-to-end latency under 2 minutes; added a dead-letter topic and replay
tooling.
• Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing
replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to approximately 25%.
• Reduced the monthly Snowflake bill from approximately 38k to approximately 24k through
warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removing unused tables.
• Mentor two mid-level data engineers, run weekly data platform office hours and participate in the
data platform on-call rotation, one week in six.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay (payments startup) | 09/2019 - 02/2022
• Built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers,
processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files from S3 daily.
• Reduced the finance team’s manual reconciliation work from approximately 3 days to
approximately 4 hours per month-end.
• Designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse with 30+ fact and dimension tables for finance and risk.
• Implemented Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables and wrote a Python
library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access used by four teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | 06/2017 - 08/2019
• Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL into an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
• Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across 40+ stores.
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science, Data Science track | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate | May 2024
COMMUNITY AND OPEN SOURCE
• Presented Data contracts without the hype at a regional data meetup in 2024.
• Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year
since 2021.
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an open-source Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug
and adding tests.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming: Python, SQL, Bash
Data engineering: Airflow, dbt, PySpark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Great Expectations,
JSON Schema
Warehouses and databases: Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic),
GitHub Actions, Git, pytest
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I have spent nine years
building and operating data systems across logistics, e-commerce and payments, with a focus
on reliable platform foundations that analysts and product teams can trust.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration for a platform with approximately
140 Airflow DAGs, and I led the migration of warehouse transformations to dbt. That work
reduced the nightly build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I also introduced
data contracts with CI checks, helped reduce broken-pipeline incidents, and built Kafka
streaming and Debezium CDC pipelines. These projects reflect the platform ownership, data
quality and reusable engineering practices described in your role.
My experience includes production-scale cloud data work on AWS, as well as Snowflake and
Redshift warehousing, Python, SQL, Docker and GitHub Actions. At Kovalent Pay, I built
PySpark reconciliation jobs on EMR and designed dimensional warehouse models for finance
and risk. I have also contributed fixes and tests to an open-source Airflow provider. My
production cloud experience is on AWS rather than Google Cloud, but it gives me a strong
foundation in operating managed data and compute services.
I am drawn to the role’s emphasis on a shared data platform and reusable frameworks for
analysts, data scientists and product teams. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my experience with platform operations, data contracts and batch and streaming systems
could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.
Kind regards, Lena Varga-Holm

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
